EXACT SCRIPT
Good morning. We're Team Braise. KFC customers already start ordering in conversation—but completing that order still sends them elsewhere. We built KFC Commerce Agent to keep the customer in chat and carry the journey through to a verified order.

text:
TIMING: 0:25-1:00

NARRATION
A high-intent customer may begin in Messenger or Zalo, but then has to switch channels, rebuild the order, check fulfillment, and wait for staff. That is where intent and commerce state drift apart. Our solution keeps the journey in one conversation while coordinating the cart, fulfillment, confirmation, and the moments where a person should step in.

EMPHASIS
Point once to TODAY and once to WITH KFC COMMERCE AGENT. Land on: One conversation. One channel. One completed order.

TRANSITION
To finish that journey safely, the system must do more than generate a helpful reply.

text:
TIMING: 1:00-1:35

NARRATION
One agent keeps a verified working state. It understands the current goal, plans the next safe action, selects bounded commerce tools, and passes policy gates before execution. After each action, it inspects the resulting state and either continues, asks for clarification, or hands off. Only successful tool results become customer-visible commerce state.

EMPHASIS
Trace: Context and goal → Plan → Select tools → Guard → Act → Verify and adapt. Do not describe a supervisor, specialist-agent system, infrastructure, model names, or raw tool names.

TRANSITION
That governed loop produces three customer-facing advantages.

text:
TIMING: 3:05-3:40

NARRATION
We designed nine representative journeys across ordering, fulfillment, payment, and recovery. For each journey, we inspect four things: was the customer outcome completed, was commerce state valid, was approval enforced, and did failure recover or hand off correctly? Logs and outcome data then feed the next cycle: observe, find gaps, improve behavior, and re-evaluate.

CLAIM BOUNDARY
Say “nine representative journeys” or “nine representative scenarios.” Do not say 9/9, all live tests pass, or imply customer research, pilot results, or measured business impact.

text:
TIMING: 3:40-4:40
ROLES: Thang controls slides and narration. Teammate operates the prepared customer-chat tab and fallback recording and does not speak.

SETUP
The customer needs food for four within a 300,000-dong budget. Watch the agent improve the basket without changing it before approval. Switch to the customer-chat tab.

TURN 1 — TEAMMATE SUBMITS
Cho mình 10 miếng gà và 4 Pepsi cỡ vừa cho 4 người, ngân sách đồ ăn 300.000đ, giao đến Big C Đồng Nai, thanh toán khi nhận hàng.

THANG
The customer starts with loose items and a budget. The agent must not change the cart before permission.
WAIT LINE IF NEEDED
The request is running; the current build does not expose internal sub-steps.
WHEN RESULT APPEARS
It found two verified combos that fit the same need and reduce the food subtotal from 404,000 to 258,000 dong—but it waits for the customer.

TURN 2 — TEAMMATE SUBMITS
Đổi sang 2 Combo Đẫy Đà 129K nhé.

THANG
With approval, the cart changes. Now it offers four large-drink upgrades for 28,000 dong and discloses the resulting price before confirmation. Do not claim the upsize is applied yet.

TURN 3 — TEAMMATE SUBMITS
Đồng ý nâng cả 4 Pepsi lên cỡ lớn. Tổng món 286.000đ, phí giao 18.000đ; xác nhận đặt đơn và thanh toán khi nhận hàng.

WHEN CONFIRMED ORDER APPEARS
The customer approved both modifications and the disclosed total. The result is one verified confirmed cash-on-delivery order. Hold for two seconds. Do not open the Operations Monitor. Return to this slide.

FALLBACK
At 18 seconds without the complete expected response and GenUI, or on any wrong recommendation, card, composition, price, saving, cart, fee, payment state, final order, error, stale session, duplicate order, or early order, teammate switches immediately to the preloaded recording. Thang says exactly: I'll switch to the recorded run of this exact scenario. Do not repair onstage or add a fourth turn.

EXACT CLOSE
Choose Team Braise to turn KFC conversations into completed orders—while keeping customers and operators in control. Stop speaking by 4:40.

text:
Q&A ONLY — DO NOT PRESENT SEQUENTIALLY

ANSWER FIRST
One request enters one governed commerce loop. The channel route starts either a synchronous chat request or durable channel run. The agent plans bounded actions, passes gates, executes tools, persists the resulting cart/order/payment state, and only then composes customer text, GenUI, and monitor events.

IF ASKED WHAT MAKES IT AGENTIC
A chatbot can generate a plausible reply. Our agent repeatedly interprets the goal, proposes next actions, selects bounded commerce tools, passes policy gates, executes them, inspects the resulting state, and adapts or hands off. Verified state changes—not text alone—define success.

BOUNDARY
This is one commerce agent loop, not a supervisor or autonomous specialist-agent team.

Q&A ONLY — DO NOT PRESENT SEQUENTIALLY

ANSWER
The model can propose a tool call or response claim, but unknown tools and invalid arguments are rejected. Safety gates require verified item codes, valid fulfillment, explicit order confirmation, and tool evidence for sensitive claims. Customer GenUI and the final response are produced from persisted tool results and commerce state.

SOURCE OF TRUTH
Persisted backend state and successful typed tool results win when the model and system disagree.

IF ASKED WHETHER IT IS MULTI-AGENT
No. It is intentionally one commerce agent loop with one state authority and one policy boundary.

BOUNDARY
The commerce clients are prototype/fixture backed; this is implemented safety design, not a production KFC system.

text:
Q&A ONLY — DO NOT PRESENT SEQUENTIALLY

NEW MESSAGE ANSWER
Channel turns are reserved, briefly coalesced, and assigned to a generation-owned run. A newer turn can supersede an older run only before an irreversible side effect. Stale responses are suppressed. Once the boundary is recorded, the system protects that execution instead of pretending it can safely rewind it.

HUMAN TAKEOVER ANSWER
The session has an explicit control state. An operator can join, which pauses AI replies; the human can respond in the same channel; then Resume AI returns control with the takeover transcript preserved.

BOUNDARY
Do not claim exactly-once delivery, production queue SLAs, or durable reconciliation after ambiguous external failures.

text:
Q&A ONLY — DO NOT PRESENT SEQUENTIALLY

ANSWER
We separate proof layers: deterministic contracts for gates and tools, scenario replay for end states, live Flutter and GenUI evidence for the customer surface, and live-model or deployed traces for runtime behavior. Logs and outcomes feed the next evaluation cycle. We never combine those layers into one misleading pass-rate number.

IF ASKED “DID ALL NINE PASS?”
They are nine representative journey designs, not a public pass-rate claim. Evidence layers are reported separately.

BOUNDARY
The nine scenarios are an engineering dataset—not user research, a pilot, or measured business impact. Do not claim all nine currently pass as live-model release tests.

text:
Q&A ONLY — DO NOT PRESENT SEQUENTIALLY

INTEGRATION ANSWER
We demonstrated the integration shape through replaceable, simulated OMS/POS adapters: typed commands, correlation, idempotency keys, status mapping, and failure handling. We have not connected to KFC production or a named vendor sandbox. Real compatibility requires authoritative contracts, credentials, test stores, webhooks, and vendor conformance evidence.

AMBIGUOUS FAILURE ANSWER
The simulated layer preserves raw OMS and POS outcomes, classifies conflicts, and attempts defined compensation where appropriate. Production deployment would require durable retries, vendor idempotency guarantees, reconciliation jobs, alerts, and an owned operations process.

BOUNDARY
Demonstrated simulated OMS/POS orchestration through replaceable adapter contracts. Do not claim KFC compatibility, restart-safe idempotency, production durability, or production readiness.
